question: When was the National Interim Government of India formed, under Jawaharlal Nehru?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2 September 1946**__.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **The Interim Government, **established on **September 2, 1946**, marked the** final phase of British colonial rule **in India.
 
• Its principal objective was to function as a transitional administration until India achieved complete independence.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru, a prominent freedom fighter and close associate of** Mahatma Gandhi,** spearheaded the Interim Government, holding the position of Vice President of the Executive Council.
 
• Key figures such as **Sardar Patel, Rajendra Prasad, and C. Rajagopalachari** were integral members of this administration.
 
• Despite its significance, the Interim Government encountered substantial challenges, including communal tensions, economic instability, and the imminent partition of India.
 
• Nevertheless, the Interim Government played a pivotal role in facilitating the transfer of power from British to Indian hands, laying the groundwork for the subsequent establishment of independent India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** was a multifaceted Indian leader, known for his roles as an anti-colonial nationalist, statesman, secular humanist, social democrat, and author.
 
• Nehru emerged as a key leader of the Indian nationalist movement in the 1930s and 1940s, advocating for India's independence from British colonial rule.
 
• Upon India's independence in 1947, Nehru assumed the position of the country's first Prime Minister, serving for an impressive 16 years.
 
• During his tenure, he championed parliamentary democracy, secularism, and advancements in science and technology, significantly influencing India's evolution as a modern nation.
 
• In the realm of international affairs, Nehru pursued a policy of non-alignment, steering India clear of alignment with the two blocs of the Cold War. Beyond his political leadership, Nehru was also a respected author.
